lean.fidelity_note: The final conclusions agree: $T_*=T_\infty>0$, the constructed Euler solution has no smooth continuation, and both integrals in (1.2) are infinite. The formal conclusion also identifies the same lifespan for every maximal solution of finite lifespan from the same datum. The explicit implication has a different preceding input: its version of Proposition 8.2 includes a uniform lower bound $c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ on every sufficiently late activation interval. The proof combines that bound with lower estimates for the crossing durations. The paper instead invokes the periodic Beale–Kato–Majda criterion after identifying the maximal time. The quantitative input is established earlier in the formal construction; it is not an unproved extra condition on the final example. This declaration proves the construction-specific corollary without proving the general continuation criterion. The integrals are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals over $[0,T_\infty)$, with essential suprema over one spatial period and operator norm for the gradient.
